content: The field of chemical nomenclature, known for its intricate and often complex naming conventions, also contains a fascinating array of peculiar and sometimes surprising names. A review of the Physical Constants of Organic Compounds section in the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics—a foundational reference—reveals not only the creative efforts of chemists but also the unusual compound names that arise from simple juxtapositions of terms. Some of these names are derived legitimately from the chemical composition of the compounds, the geographic regions where they are found, the plant or animal species from which they are isolated, or the names of their discoverers. Others are intentionally given unusual or whimsical trivial names based on their molecular structure, a notable property, or simply the personal preferences of the chemists who first isolated them. However, many trivial names predate the establishment of formal naming conventions. Trivial names can sometimes be ambiguous or carry different meanings depending on the industry, geographic region, or language in which they are used. As Godley observed, Trivial names having the status of INN (International Nonproprietary Names) or ISO (International Organization for Standardization) are carefully tailored for their field of use and are internationally accepted. In his preface to Chemical Nomenclature, Thurlow remarked that Chemical names do not have to be deadly serious. Since 1997, a classic website maintained at the University of Bristol has curated a selection of molecules with silly or unusual names, primarily for entertainment purposes. These so-called silly or funny trivial names, which may vary in perception depending on cultural context, can also serve an educational purpose. In an article published in the Journal of Chemical Education, Dennis Ryan argued that students learning organic nomenclature—a subject often considered dry and uninteresting—might develop a genuine interest when tasked with converting funny-sounding trivial names into their proper systematic equivalents. The collection presented below offers a sample of such trivial names, providing insight into the creativity of chemists when coining new names for chemical compounds outside the bounds of systematic nomenclature. It also includes examples of systematic names and acronyms that coincidentally resemble English words.
